sources.title: NCERT Mathematics Textbook for Class IX (rationalised) with the CBSE Secondary Curriculum syllabus for Mathematics (Code 041)
sources.issuingAuthority: National Council of Educational Research and Training / Central Board of Secondary Education
sources.edition: Rationalised edition in force for session 2026-27
sources.officialReference: https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php (Class IX Mathematics) and https://cbseacademic.nic.in/curriculum.html (Secondary Curriculum, Mathematics 041)
sources.licensing: Structure, chapter titles and syllabus weightings are cited as factual curriculum metadata. No textbook text, figures or exercise items are copied or stored in this repository. All questions in the pack are original EduOS material.

ambiguities: Unit mark weights follow the CBSE Class 9 Mathematics syllabus split (Number Systems 10, Algebra 20, Coordinate Geometry 4, Geometry 27, Mensuration 13, Statistics 6 = 80). A subject expert must confirm the 2026-27 circular before any activation.
Chapter list assumes the rationalised 12-chapter NCERT structure (Constructions, Areas of Parallelograms and Triangles, and Probability removed). Reviewer must confirm no reinstatement for 2026-27.

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 1: Number Systems

outcomes.title: Classify real numbers as rational or irrational and place them on the number line

atoms.text: Recognise a rational number as p/q with q ≠ 0 and integers p, q
Identify non-terminating non-recurring decimals as irrational

outcomes.title: Apply the laws of exponents for real bases and rationalise simple denominators

atoms.text: Simplify expressions using a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) and (a^m)^n = a^(mn)
Rationalise a denominator of the form 1/(a + √b)

topics.title: Squares, cubes and estimation of roots

outcomes.title: Estimate and verify square roots and cube roots of numbers using known perfect powers

atoms.text: Estimate the square root of a non-perfect-square number using nearby perfect squares
Estimate the cube root of a non-perfect-cube number using nearby perfect cubes

topics.title: Representing real numbers on the number line

outcomes.title: Locate rational and irrational numbers on the number line using geometric and successive magnification methods

atoms.text: Represent √n geometrically using the Pythagoras theorem construction on a number line
Locate a given decimal number between two points using successive magnification

outcomes.title: Perform addition, subtraction, multiplication and division involving rational and irrational numbers correctly

atoms.text: Add or subtract two surds after expressing them with the same irrational part
Determine whether the sum, difference, product or quotient of a rational and an irrational number is rational or irrational

topics.title: Laws of exponents for real numbers

outcomes.title: Use the laws of exponents to simplify expressions involving rational exponents and negative powers

atoms.text: Simplify expressions using a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n) and (ab)^m = a^m × b^m
Evaluate expressions with zero and negative rational exponents

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 2: Polynomials

outcomes.title: Determine the degree of a polynomial and verify whether a value is a zero

atoms.text: State the degree of a polynomial in one variable
Evaluate p(a) to test whether a is a zero of p(x)

outcomes.title: Factorise quadratic and cubic expressions using standard identities and the factor theorem

atoms.text: Use (a + b)² , (a − b)² and a² − b² to factorise
Apply the factor theorem to factorise a cubic polynomial

topics.title: Remainder theorem and value of polynomials

outcomes.title: Apply the remainder theorem to find remainders and use it to check factors

atoms.text: Use the remainder theorem to find the remainder of p(x) on division by (x − a)
Use the remainder/factor theorem to test whether (x − a) is a factor of p(x)

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 4: Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Solutions of a linear equation in two variables

outcomes.title: Express a linear equation in the form ax + by + c = 0 and find its solutions

atoms.text: Write a statement as a linear equation in two variables
Verify that an ordered pair satisfies a linear equation

outcomes.title: Draw and interpret the graph of a linear equation in two variables

atoms.text: Plot at least two solutions and join them to graph the equation
Interpret intercepts of the line with the axes

outcomes.title: Solve real-life problems using linear equations in two variables and represent them graphically

atoms.text: Find the common solution of two linear equations in two variables
Translate a word problem into a pair of linear equations and interpret the graph

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 3: Coordinate Geometry

topics.title: The Cartesian plane and plotting points

outcomes.title: Plot points in the Cartesian plane and identify quadrants and axes

atoms.text: Name the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates
Identify points lying on the x-axis or y-axis

outcomes.title: Describe the axes, origin and coordinates of a point in the Cartesian plane

atoms.text: State the names given to the horizontal and vertical reference lines
State the coordinates of the point where the axes meet

outcomes.title: Determine the quadrant of a point using the sign pattern of its coordinates

atoms.text: Match the sign combination (+,+), (-,+), (-,-), (+,-) to quadrants I, II, III, IV
Decide the quadrant of a point given only its sign pattern

outcomes.title: Plot given ordered pairs and read off coordinates of marked points on a grid

atoms.text: Locate a point on a squared grid given its ordered pair
Write the ordered pair for a point already marked on a grid

topics.title: Points on the axes and distances along an axis

outcomes.title: Identify points lying on the axes and compute distances between points sharing an axis value

atoms.text: Recognise that points on the x-axis have y-coordinate 0 and points on the y-axis have x-coordinate 0
Find the distance between two points that lie on the same horizontal or vertical line

topics.title: Graphs of linear equations of the form y = mx

outcomes.title: Draw and interpret the graph of a linear equation of the form y = mx passing through the origin

atoms.text: Generate a table of values for y = mx and use it to plot the line
Check whether a given point satisfies an equation of the form y = mx

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 5: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry

outcomes.title: Distinguish Euclid's axioms from his postulates and use them in simple reasoning

atoms.text: State Euclid's five postulates
Use the axiom 'things equal to the same thing are equal to one another'

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 6: Lines and Angles

outcomes.title: Use linear pair, vertically opposite and transversal angle relations to find unknown angles

atoms.text: Apply the linear pair axiom (angles on a straight line sum to 180°)
Use corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles for parallel lines

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 7: Triangles

outcomes.title: Select and justify the correct congruence criterion (SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS)

atoms.text: Match given data to the appropriate congruence rule
Recognise that SSA is not a valid congruence criterion

outcomes.title: Apply angle-sum, isosceles-triangle and triangle-inequality properties

atoms.text: Use the angle sum property of a triangle (180°)
Compare sides and opposite angles using the triangle inequality

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 8: Quadrilaterals

outcomes.title: Use and justify the defining properties of a parallelogram and its special cases

atoms.text: Opposite sides and opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal
Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other

outcomes.title: Apply the midpoint theorem and its converse in a triangle or quadrilateral

atoms.text: The segment joining midpoints of two sides is parallel to and half the third side
Use the converse to locate a midpoint

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 9: Circles

outcomes.title: Relate chords, their distances from the centre, and the angles they subtend

atoms.text: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at any point on the remaining arc

outcomes.title: Use the cyclic-quadrilateral angle property and its converse

atoms.text: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary
Angles in the same segment are equal

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 10: Heron's Formula

topics.title: Area of triangles using Heron's formula

outcomes.title: Compute areas of triangles and composite figures using Heron's formula

atoms.text: Compute the semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2
Apply Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c))

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 11: Surface Areas and Volumes

outcomes.title: Calculate curved and total surface areas of cones, cylinders and spheres

atoms.text: Apply CSA of a cylinder = 2πrh and of a cone = πrl
Apply surface area of a sphere = 4πr²

outcomes.title: Calculate volumes of cylinders, cones and spheres and solve capacity problems

atoms.text: Apply volume of a cylinder = πr²h and of a cone = ⅓πr²h
Convert between cm³ and litres in capacity problems

topics.title: Surface area and volume of cuboids and cubes

outcomes.title: Calculate surface area and volume of cuboids and cubes and solve related problems

atoms.text: Apply total surface area of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl) and of a cube = 6a²
Apply volume of a cuboid = l × b × h and of a cube = a³

topics.title: Surface area and volume of hemispheres

outcomes.title: Calculate curved and total surface area and volume of a hemisphere

atoms.text: Apply CSA of a hemisphere = 2πr² and TSA = 3πr²
Apply volume of a hemisphere = (2/3)πr³

topics.title: Applied capacity and cost problems on solids

outcomes.title: Solve real-life problems involving capacity, material cost and painting of solids

atoms.text: Convert volume to capacity in litres and compute cost using a given rate
Combine surface area formulae to compute the cost of painting or covering composite solids

provenance.note: NCERT Class IX Mathematics, Chapter 12: Statistics

outcomes.title: Organise raw data into frequency tables and read bar graphs and histograms

atoms.text: Build a grouped frequency distribution with equal class intervals
Read values from a histogram or bar graph

outcomes.title: Compute and interpret mean, median and mode of ungrouped data

atoms.text: Compute the mean as the sum of observations divided by their number
Find the median of an even and an odd number of observations
